status: DRAFT 2026-11-05. Literature-based proxy key: what published sources say about each candidate column, per attribute. Complements the measured key (compas_proxies.json).

labels.proxy: the column can reveal who someone is (their race, sex or age); identity proxy
labels.contested: sources disagree whether the column is a proxy for the attribute
labels.correlated: sources report a correlation with the attribute without calling the column a proxy
labels.tainted: sources say the column's values are shaped by discrimination against the group (biased measurement), not that it reveals identity

scoring_sets.literature_any: labels: proxy, contested, correlated, tainted (any documented fairness concern linking the column to the attribute)

cfpb_bisg.cite: CFPB, BISG proxy methodology (surname and geography), public code

bisg_2022.cite: How should we proxy for race/ethnicity? Comparing BISG to machine learning methods (2022)

fryer_levitt_2004.cite: Fryer & Levitt (2004), The Causes and Consequences of Distinctively Black Names, QJE

bertrand_mullainathan_2004.cite: Bertrand & Mullainathan (2004), Are Emily and Greg More Employable than Lakisha and Jamal?, AER

santamaria_2018.cite: Santamaria & Mihaljevic (2018), Comparison and benchmark of name-to-gender inference services, PeerJ CS

harcourt_2010.cite: Harcourt (2010), Risk as a Proxy for Race

mayson_2019.cite: Mayson (2019), Bias In, Bias Out, Yale Law Journal 128

rudin_2020.cite: Rudin, Wang & Coker (2020), The Age of Secrecy and Unfairness in Recidivism Prediction, HDSR

aclu_2013.cite: ACLU (2013), The War on Marijuana in Black and White

rehavi_starr_2014.cite: Rehavi & Starr (2014), Racial Disparity in Federal Criminal Sentences, JPE
